All original text is present, with zero-based original span markers <SPAN i>...</SPAN i>. For supported/opposed hypotheses cite all original evidence span indices for that decision, including independently operative redundant support and necessary governing language. For NotMentioned return an empty evidence list. Treat conditions and exceptions within scope, and distinguish limited permission from universal permission. Give a short public reason (at most 15 words per hypothesis). Do not execute further tools, invent citations or rewrite span indices. Return exactly the supplied JSON schema with all 17 original hypothesis keys. For each emit choice, spans, reason in that order. The common schema describes permitted values, not answers about this contract. Evidence candidates are fallible, not mandatory citations; make every final label and evidence decision yourself from the complete original contract. The complete original NDA remains present and unchanged. Each hypothesis has fallible_evidence_candidates from a fixed ordinary retriever, plus additional_source_read_indices obtained by literal source access. Both resolve to exact original text in candidate_original_text. Additional indices omit duplicate ordinary candidates, not low-scoring facts. These are reading aids, never a verdict or mandatory evidence. Scores describe fallible evidence membership, not legal confidence. No skill identities, query counts or scope-control map are supplied. Optional evidence_selection_criteria are fallible learned inspection procedures for that hypothesis, never contract facts, label verdicts or mandatory citations. Literal access roles describe how a location was reached, not whether it is evidence. Empty leads never mean NotMentioned. Read the full source, reject irrelevant material and cite ANY original index as needed, including outside every lead. Decide the exact original hypothesis yourself; do not substitute another hypothesis. Return choice, spans and reason only.

<SPAN 2>(Non-Standard)</SPAN 2>
<SPAN 3>This Non-Disclosure Agreement ("Agreement") is between County of Orange (“County”) and Microsoft Corporation and its affiliates (“Microsoft”) as indicated in the signature block below. </SPAN 3><SPAN 4>The County and Microsoft may be referred to individually as “Party” or collectively as “Parties.” </SPAN 4><SPAN 5>“We,” “us” and “our” refer to both of the Parties signing below and the Parties’ respective affiliates.</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>COMPANY AND ITS AFFILIATES or INDIVIDUAL: MICROSOFT CORPORATION</SPAN 6>
<SPAN 7>County of Orange, a political subdivision of the State of</SPAN 7>
<SPAN 8>AND ITS AFFILIATES</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>California</SPAN 9>
<SPAN 10>Address: 333 W. Santa Ana Blvd. One Microsoft </SPAN 10><SPAN 11>Way</SPAN 11>

<SPAN 19>Signature Date: Signature Date:</SPAN 19>
<SPAN 20>Expiration Date of this Agreement: </SPAN 20><SPAN 21>This Agreement expires one hundred and eighty (180) days from the later of the two signature dates above, unless an earlier date is stated in the limited purpose that follows.</SPAN 21>
<SPAN 22>Limited Purpose: Application of this Agreement is limited to the following transaction or other interaction between the parties:</SPAN 22>
<SPAN 23>Participation in the County of Orange HRS Data Analytics Project – Phase </SPAN 23><SPAN 24>I and development of the associated Enterprise-wide Business Intelligence Platform.</SPAN 24>
<SPAN 25>Corporate and External Legal Affairs (CELA) Contact: Charlie Bingham (CELA)</SPAN 25>
<SPAN 26>1. The purpose of this Agreement. </SPAN 26><SPAN 27>This Agreement allows us to disclose Confidential Information (defined below) to each other, to our own affiliates and to the other’s affiliates, under the following terms. </SPAN 27><SPAN 28>An “affiliate” is any legal entity that one of us owns, that owns one of us or that is under common control with one of us. </SPAN 28><SPAN 29>“Control” and “own” mean possessing a 50% or greater interest in an entity or the right to direct the management of the entity. </SPAN 29><SPAN 30>Additionally we may disclose the other’s Confidential Information to our respective Representatives (as defined herein below) only if those Representatives are required to have the Confidential Information for the purposes in this Agreement. </SPAN 30><SPAN 31>Before doing so, each Party must ensure that affiliates and Representatives are required to protect the Confidential Information on terms consistent with this Agreement.</SPAN 31>
<SPAN 32>2. Confidential information.</SPAN 32>
<SPAN 33>Microsoft Filing Instructions: after both parties sign and date this Agreement, Your customer should retain one original for their files and return the other to you. </SPAN 33><SPAN 34>Then, address the second original to:</SPAN 34>
<SPAN 35>NDA, CRM 124/Records</SPAN 35>
<SPAN 36>Microsoft Corporation</SPAN 36>
<SPAN 37>1 Microsoft Way</SPAN 37>
<SPAN 38>Redmond, WA 98052-6399</SPAN 38>
<SPAN 39> </SPAN 39><SPAN 40>IEAID:243659</SPAN 40>
<SPAN 41>a. What is included. </SPAN 41><SPAN 42>"Confidential Information" is non-public information, know-how and trade secrets in any form that:</SPAN 42>
<SPAN 43> A. </SPAN 43><SPAN 44>Are designated in writing as “confidential” at the time of their disclosure and include: </SPAN 44><SPAN 45>(1) corporate financial records or corporate proprietary information (e.g. trade secrets) exempted under the California Public Records Act, California Government Code Sections 6250, et seq.; or </SPAN 45><SPAN 46>(2) information that a reasonable person knows or reasonably should understand to be confidential, and is treated confidential by the disclosing party.</SPAN 46>
<SPAN 47> B. </SPAN 47><SPAN 48>The County’s sensitive security information, or technical data, programs, software (including configuration or source codes), technical information, screen shots, customer information, employee records, computer network, architectural or engineering information, exploitable data, information protected by privacy law, or other information that is treated as confidential by the County, or is prohibited from being disclosed for any reason pursuant to law, statute, regulation, ordinance, or contract.</SPAN 48>
<SPAN 49>b. What is not included. </SPAN 49><SPAN 50>The following types of information, however marked, are not Confidential Information. </SPAN 50><SPAN 51>Information that:</SPAN 51>
<SPAN 52> Is, or becomes, publicly available without a breach of this Agreement or through no fault of the recipient of the information;</SPAN 52>
<SPAN 53> Is or becomes lawfully known to the recipient of the information without an obligation to keep it confidential;</SPAN 53>
<SPAN 54> Is received from another source who can disclose it lawfully;</SPAN 54>
<SPAN 55> Is independently developed;</SPAN 55>
<SPAN 56> Is a comment or suggestion one of the Parties volunteers about the other’s business, products or services;</SPAN 56>
<SPAN 57> Is in the recipient’s possession before receipt from the discloser of the information;</SPAN 57>
<SPAN 58> Is disclosed by the recipient with the discloser’s prior written approval; or</SPAN 58>
<SPAN 59> Is disclosed by court order or under operation of applicable law including, but not limited to, the California Public Records Act, California Government Code Sections 6250, et seq.</SPAN 59>
<SPAN 60>3. Treatment of Confidential Information.</SPAN 60>
<SPAN 61>a. In general. </SPAN 61><SPAN 62>Subject to the other terms of this Agreement, each of us agrees:</SPAN 62>
<SPAN 63> Except as required under any court order or law including, but not limited to, the California Public Records Act and Ralph M. Brown Act (California Government Code section 54950 et seq.), subpoena, or any other legally permitted or required disclosure, the Parties agree not to disclose the other’s Confidential Information to third parties except to those employees of a recipient who are required to have the information for the purposes in this Agreement, Representatives (defined below), and except as otherwise allowed in this Agreement; and</SPAN 63>
<SPAN 64> The Parties will use and disclose the other’s Confidential Information only for purposes of evaluating and engaging in an actual or potential business relationship with each other.</SPAN 64>
<SPAN 65>b. Security precautions. </SPAN 65><SPAN 66>Each Party agrees:</SPAN 66>
<SPAN 67> To take reasonable steps to protect the other Party’s Confidential Information. </SPAN 67><SPAN 68>These steps must be at least as protective as those we take to protect our own Confidential Information of a similar nature;</SPAN 68>
<SPAN 69> To notify the other promptly upon discovery of any unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information; and</SPAN 69>
<SPAN 70> To cooperate with the other to help regain control of the Confidential Information and prevent further unauthorized use or disclosure of it.</SPAN 70>
<SPAN 71>c. Sharing Confidential Information with affiliates and Representatives.</SPAN 71>
<SPAN 72> For the purposes of this Agreement, a “Representative” is an employee, contractor, vendor, service provider, advisor or consultant of a Party or a Party’s respective affiliates including, but not limited to, Science Applications International Corporation (“SAIC”) and Atos Governmental IT Outsourcing Services, LLC (“Atos”) and each of their respective employees, affiliates, and subcontractors.</SPAN 72>
<SPAN 73> Each Party may disclose the other’s Confidential Information to its Representatives (who may then disclose that Confidential Information to other of its Representatives) only if those Representatives are required to have the Confidential Information for the purposes in this Agreement. </SPAN 73><SPAN 74>Before doing so, each Party must ensure that affiliates and Representatives are required to protect the Confidential Information on terms consistent with this Agreement.</SPAN 74>
<SPAN 75> Neither Party is required to restrict work assignments of Representatives who have had access to Confidential Information. </SPAN 75><SPAN 76>Each Party acknowledges that they cannot control the incoming information the other Party will disclose in the course of the business relationship between the Parties, or what each Party’s Representatives will remember, even without notes or other aids. </SPAN 76><SPAN 77>Each Party agrees that use of information in its Representatives’ unaided memories in the development or deployment of the Parties’ respective products or services does not create liability for that Party under this Agreement or trade secret law. </SPAN 77><SPAN 78>Both Parties mutually agree to limit what each Party discloses to the other accordingly.</SPAN 78>
<SPAN 79>d. Disclosing Confidential Information if required to by law. </SPAN 79><SPAN 80>Each Party may disclose the other’s Confidential Information if required to comply with a court order, law, or other government demand that has the force of law including, but not limited to, the California Public Records Act, California Government Code section 6250 et seq. </SPAN 80><SPAN 81>If a Party is required to disclose the other Party’s Confidential Information pursuant to applicable law, statute, or regulation, or court order, that Party will give to the other written notice of the order or request mandating disclosure of the Confidential Information in order to provide a reasonable opportunity for the other Party to object to such disclosure of its Confidential Information and seek a protective order or appropriate remedy. </SPAN 81><SPAN 82>If, in the absence of a protective order, the recipient determines that it is required to disclose such information, it may disclose without breach of this Agreement only Confidential Information specifically required and only to the extent compelled to do so .</SPAN 82>
<SPAN 83>By entering into this Agreement, Microsoft expressly acknowledges that the County is a government entity subject to the California Public Records Act. </SPAN 83><SPAN 84>If the County receives a request pursuant to the California Public Records Act for Confidential Information that Microsoft has designated as “confidential” in writing, the County will notify Microsoft of the request, so that Microsoft can seek protection from disclosure by a court of competent jurisdiction. </SPAN 84><SPAN 85>Notwithstanding any other provisions of this Agreement, the County may in its discretion disclose Microsoft’s Confidential Information in the County’s possession without breach of this Agreement if the County notifies Microsoft of the pending California Public Records Act request and Microsoft fails to seek and obtain protection from disclosure by a court of competent jurisdiction.</SPAN 85>
<SPAN 86>4. Length of Confidential Information obligations. </SPAN 86><SPAN 87>Except as permitted above and unless otherwise required by applicable law or court order, neither Party will use or disclose the other’s Confidential Information for five years after it is received. </SPAN 87><SPAN 88>The five-year time period does not apply if applicable law requires a longer period. </SPAN 88><SPAN 89>This duty to withhold Confidential Information survives any expiration or termination of this Agreement as provided herein.</SPAN 89>
<SPAN 90>5. General rights and obligations.</SPAN 90>
<SPAN 91>a. Law that applies; jurisdiction and venue. </SPAN 91><SPAN 92>This Agreement has been negotiated and executed in the State of California and shall be governed by and construed under the laws of the State of California, without reference to conflicts of law provisions. </SPAN 92><SPAN 93>In the event of any legal action to enforce or interpret this Agreement, the sole and exclusive venue shall be a court of competent jurisdiction located in Orange County, California, and the Parties hereto agree to and do hereby submit to the jurisdiction of such court, notwithstanding California Code of Civil Procedure section 394. </SPAN 93><SPAN 94>Furthermore, the Parties specifically agree to waive any and all rights to request that an action be transferred for trial to another county.</SPAN 94>
<SPAN 95>b. Compliance with law. </SPAN 95><SPAN 96>Each of us will comply with all export laws that apply to Confidential Information.</SPAN 96>
<SPAN 97>c. Waiver. </SPAN 97><SPAN 98>Any delay or failure of either of us to exercise a right or remedy will not result in a waiver of that, or any other, right or remedy.</SPAN 98>
<SPAN 99>d. Money damages insufficient. </SPAN 99><SPAN 100>Each of us acknowledges that money damages may not be sufficient compensation for a breach of this Agreement. </SPAN 100><SPAN 101>Each of us agrees that the other may seek court orders to stop Confidential Information from becoming public in breach of this Agreement.</SPAN 101>
<SPAN 102>e. Transfers of this Agreement. </SPAN 102><SPAN 103>If one of us transfers this Agreement, we will not disclose the other’s Confidential Information to the transferee without the other’s consent.</SPAN 103>
<SPAN 104>f. Enforceability. </SPAN 104><SPAN 105>If any provision of this Agreement is unenforceable, the parties (or, if we cannot agree, a court) will revise it so that it can be enforced. </SPAN 105><SPAN 106>Even if no revision is possible, the rest of this Agreement will remain in place.</SPAN 106>
<SPAN 107>g. Entire agreement. </SPAN 107><SPAN 108>This Agreement does not grant any implied intellectual property licenses to Confidential Information, except as stated above. </SPAN 108><SPAN 109>We may have contracts with each other covering other specific aspects of our relationship (“other contracts”). </SPAN 109><SPAN 110>The other contract may include commitments about Confidential Information, either within it or by referencing another non-disclosure agreement. </SPAN 110><SPAN 111>If so, those obligations remain in place for purposes of that other contract. </SPAN 111><SPAN 112>With this exception, this is the entire agreement between us regarding Confidential Information. </SPAN 112><SPAN 113>It replaces all other agreements and understandings regarding Confidential Information. </SPAN 113><SPAN 114>We can only change this Agreement with a signed document that states that it is changing this Agreement.</SPAN 114>
